nodes.summary: Let $B$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $L$, let $\mathfrak{q}$ be a height-one prime of $B$, and let $w$ be a valuation on $L$ with values in the multiplicative group $\mathbb{Z}$ with a zero adjoined. Suppose that $w(b) \le 1$ for every $b \in B$, and that for every $b \in B$ we have $b \in \mathfrak{q}$ if and only if $w(b) < 1$. Then the $\mathfrak{q}$-adic valuation of $L$ is equivalent to $w$.
nodes.title: A valuation centered at a height-one prime is equivalent to its adic valuation

nodes.title: Each extension of a prime-adic valuation comes from exactly one prime above

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, let $L$ be a field extension of $K$, and let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a height-one prime of $A$. A valuation $w$ on $L$ with values in the multiplicative group $\mathbb{Z}$ with a zero adjoined extends the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic valuation of $K$ when its restriction to $K$ is equivalent to the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic valuation of $K$.
nodes.title: Valuations extending a prime-adic valuation

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind domains with $B$ an $A$-algebra, let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a height-one prime of $A$, and let $\mathfrak{q}$ be a height-one prime of $B$ lying over $\mathfrak{p}$. Then for every $a \in A$, $a \in \mathfrak{p}$ if and only if the image of $a$ in $B$ lies in $\mathfrak{q}$.
nodes.title: Membership in a prime is detected by a prime lying over it

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind domains with $B$ an $A$-algebra, and let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a height-one prime of $A$. The primes above $\mathfrak{p}$ form the set of height-one primes $\mathfrak{q}$ of $B$ lying over $\mathfrak{p}$, that is, whose preimage in $A$ is $\mathfrak{p}$.
nodes.title: Height-one primes above a prime

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
